turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this computer's crawling again. What's brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing, really. I nearly didn't come. Just a niggle in the left side, the loin, went down to the groin.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hang on, wrong window. Uh, say that again?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Left loin, shooting to the groin. Woke me about two this morning. It's eased. I wouldn't call it severe.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nought to ten, worst and right now?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm a four. Well actually a seven, maybe an eight, just for a few minutes. Now it's a two. Hardly there.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Were you sick?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, threw up the once in the night. Nothing since. Doesn't count.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood in the urine?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Wee was a bit pink this morning. Not blood, a tinge. Probably the light.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll read the dipstick. Blood three plus, protein trace, leucocytes negative, nitrites negative, glucose negative.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Three plus. They love a drama.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Obs from just now, temp 36.7, pulse 88, blood pressure 152 over 94, sats 97 percent. Left loin is tender, tummy soft, no guarding.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Only sore when you press. Rest of it is normal, like I said.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever or shivers, or stinging when you pass water?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Neither.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain on the right side at all?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest, breathing, all alright?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, fine.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medicines? Sorry, say it clearly, I clicked the cricket by mistake. No, I'm listening.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Just amlodopine, 5 milligrams every morning, for the blood pressure. Years. Nothing else.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None at all.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, while this request screen loads, have you seen the test? England are 240 for 4, Root's timing is lovely.

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Had it on the radio till the traffic got me. The A38 was a car park, a good hour. Bloke said it's glorious out, proper shirt-sleeve weather. My neighbour's grandson has a club match Saturday if it holds, and I was more fed up about missing the morning session than anything.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ha. I might get the mower out if clinic ever ends. Lovely day for it. Sorry, screen's back.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): You're alright. I'm wasting your time anyway.

[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): I don't think you are. You've got the high blood pressure, I know. My impression is renal colic, likely a stone, but that's provisional, the scan has to confirm it. I'll start naproxen, 500 milligrams twice a day by mouth, with food, for five days, from today.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): If you insist. Seems a lot for a niggle.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse takes your bloods at eleven this morning, full blood count and kidney function. No need to fast, just drink some water beforehand. And a non-contrast CT of the kidneys is booked for two this afternoon.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Both today? Blimey.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): If those bloods are borderline we'll add a serum calcium, not otherwise. I'll see you back here in two weeks.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks is fine. I'll be right as rain.

spec.situation: Sudden severe loin pain going to the groin overnight, vomiting once, blood in urine; pain score given loosely; urine dip result read aloud; painkiller and scan planned today.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Urine dipstick results not fully recorded: blood 3+, protein trace, leucocytes negative, nitrites negative, glucose negative.
Negative finding asked and answered: no shivers.
Pain severity was also described as 4/10 before being revised to 7-8/10 briefly; recorded symptoms omit this qualifier.
Pain had eased and the patient said they would not call it severe / was hardly there now.
Possible right-sided pain was mentioned ambiguously ('Sometimes, not really'); this uncertainty is not recorded.
